Delta review of the merge of main (`db091cb38`) into this branch. It relies on the clean collaborator review of head `6c458ec1f6072a2523bbe958bd4b065145ab4482`. The delta class is DELTA. I did not review the whole PR again.

Verdict: the merge is clean. Ready for the maintainer to merge when the draft state is lifted.

What I checked in the merge:
- `git show --remerge-diff` shows one hand-resolved file: `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs`. There is no other hand edit.
- The resolution takes the PR's test `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette` in place of main's `the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name` (#1709). The Gate map header is intact (lines 1-14).
- `git diff origin/main...02892e348 --stat` shows only the PR's 10 files. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not changed. No `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs` or workflow change.

Safety of the replaced test:
- Main pinned a refusal because the sample's silhouette strip is 6.53 mm wide. The PR changes the footprint law on purpose. The decision record `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md` explains the change and names this test. The replacement is justified.
- The new test (`shared_face_bodies.rs:174-182`) asserts only that status is `ok`. It does not call `verify`. The no-gouge proof is in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_open_side.rs` (`assert_no_gouge`, lines 164-190, 224) and in the neighbour and live-post tests. The sample itself is not checked for gouge. This is not blocking. A suggested follow-up: add the `gate_problems` no-gouge assert, as the 3D Finish test in the same file does at line 162.
- Main's new commits do not change `pocket3d`, `open_side`, `keep_law` or `kept_rejudge` in a way that interacts with this PR. All the suites below pass on the merged tree.

Results on the merged head, locally in the review worktree (debug):

| Suite | Passed | Ignored |
|---|---:|---:|
| app: shared_face_bodies | 5 | 1 |
| app: pocket3d_open_side | 5 | 0 |
| app: keep_law | 8 | 0 |
| app: neighbour_law | 6 | 0 |
| motion: pocket_refusal | 3 | 0 |

No failures. Clippy on camcraft-app and camcraft-motion with `--all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. I did not run the full quick gate, the UI suites or the ignored tests. No GitHub runner was used.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 02892e348b8504c46f3e70e709ac837f14978f43 -->
Full independent review of the change of this PR (diff `origin/main...02892e348`, 10 files). The earlier full review was by the author's own account. The merge-time delta review stands and is not repeated.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The code looks sound. The claim "the sample verifies clean" is wrong, and the test for it is too weak.

## What looks good
- `machining3d::open_sides` (`crates/motion/src/machining3d/open_side.rs:35-41`) is small and safe. It uses no `unwrap`, no `expect` and no `panic!`. A non-finite or too small growth returns the silhouette unchanged. Errors propagate as `GenError`.
- The reasoning in `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md` holds. Outside the model's silhouette no model material stands at any Z. The grown band is cut by the other parts' silhouettes. The level law still erodes by the full radius from the part section at each level. So the cutter edge passes the silhouette by at most R less 0.01 mm, and only where the level is open. I found no path where the new footprint cuts the model.
- Scope is narrow: only a source-built, untilted, whole-model footprint (`operation/open_side.rs:23-25`). A picked or Boundary region and a tilted plane are unchanged.
- The neighbour parts now reach the solid law (`keep_law.rs`, `is_part_kept_kind`). This is a sound second net. `kept_rejudge` shares the same rule, so the live post check agrees with generation.
- `pocket3d_open_side.rs` is a good synthetic proof: stock measured at the floor along both open edges, no feed disc in the model, a neighbour kept out, and the solid-law warning. The PR text lists its mutation checks.
- Layers, crate placement, Gate maps and provenance lines are correct. The new files are under 400 lines. No snapshot PNG changes. No process files changed. No `CHANGELOG.md` edit. `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1749` are present.

## Results (locally, merged state of the head; main checks were done in the delta review)
In addition to the suites already green today (app `shared_face_bodies` 5 passed 1 ignored, `pocket3d_open_side` 5, `keep_law` 8, `neighbour_law` 6, motion `pocket_refusal` 3, clippy on app and motion):
- motion lib 366 passed, 5 ignored; `center_cut_law` 6; `islands_model_fault` 2; `level_links` 12; `machining3d` 23; `multiaxis_rough` 5; `one_descent` 3; `pocket3d_hsm` 3 (1 ignored); `refusal_ghost` 3; `stock_seam` 1.
- app `operations` 119 (6 ignored); `whole_model_pocket` 5 (1 ignored); `pocket3d_hsm` 1 (1 ignored); `solid_law` 4; `kept_parts_live` 4; `coarse_laws` 6; `center_cut_multiaxis` 6; `level_links` 7; `pocket_overhead` 2; `area_controls` 13.
- Not run: the rest of the quick-gate app list, the ui suites (`operations`, `boundary_picks` and others) and the ignored heavy lanes. The PR text also names these as not run.

Scratch check on the real sample (not committed, removed): I added a `verify` call after `generate R1` on the as-imported sample. With S1 present, `verify` skips the gate ("an operation is stale or never generated"). With S1 deleted, `gate.ok` is true and `gate.problems` is empty. But `findings` holds 306 `shank_hit` and 30 `rapid_in_stock`, all `blocks_post: true`, all on R1. The same check on the laid-flat sample gives no findings.

## Requested before merge
1. `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs:174-182`, the doc comment at `:165-172` and the PR body and decision file say the sample pocket "verifies clean". The test asserts only `status == "ok"`. The real reading is that `verify` reports 336 findings that block the post (shank and holder hits, rapids below the clearance plane inside stock). There is no gouge finding, and the post is not silently wrong, but the op reads `ok` while its toolpath cannot post. Do one of these:
   - Add a `verify` step to the test (delete S1 first, or generate it, so the gate is not skipped). Assert `gate.ok`, no `gouge` problem, and the findings you expect. If the shank hits are real (6 mm tool, about 118 mm of depth) or come from the open-side reach, say so in the test and the decision file, or make the op refuse or warn.
   - Or correct the text: drop "verifies clean" and name the blocking findings as an owed item with its own issue.
2. `shared_face_bodies` runs in the default suite and takes about 30 s for this test. Check the budget with the added `verify` step. If it passes 60 s in debug, move it to the heavy lane.

## Questions and notes (not blocking)
- The open footprint assumes that nothing but the model and the setup's other parts stands outside the silhouette. Fixtures (vise jaws) are not in the keep-out. The decision file does not say this. Please add one line, so a later fixture law can find it.
- `generate.rs` is 3668 lines, over the 400-line guide. This PR adds 11. Not blocking.
- The tilted 3+2 case keeps the old law, as the PR says. A follow-up issue would help if none exists.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 82c9f082b5297ee3da2cbd833e91028a6b7d337b -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a delta review of the commits after `02892e348`. The earlier full review of that head stands for the rest: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1772#pullrequestreview-5910347140

## What changed since the full review
`git diff 02892e348..82c9f082b` touches two files only: `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs` and `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md`. No file in `crates/*/src` changed.

## What looks good
- The test `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette` now pins the true behaviour. It asserts: R1 status `ok`; the gate ran and passed; no `gouge` problem; every finding is `shank_hit` or `rapid_in_stock`; each finding is on R1 with `blocks_post: true`; each `shank_hit` says "collides with the part"; `ok: false`; `held_by == ["R1"]`.
- The test is strict enough. A gouge, a finding of another kind, or a non-blocking finding fails it. It also requires at least one of each kind. It ignores the exact counts. This is acceptable, because the kinds, the op and the blocking flag are exact. The decision file says why.
- Deleting S1 is legitimate. The test comment cites #1840: an S1 that never generated skips the program gate. The test checks that the gate ran (`gate.skipped` absent). The delete removes no check on R1.
- The second half gives the tool 125 mm flutes and a 6 mm shank, generates again and asserts `ok: true` with no findings. This shows that the findings come from the tool reach and not from the #1749 footprint.
- The decision file now says the fixtures are not in the keep-out. It also says that the fixture laws of verify still block a cut into a jaw. This closes my earlier note.
- The text "verifies clean" is removed from the doc comment, the decision file and the PR body. The three texts agree with the test.

## Results merged with main
Run locally in the existing worktree at this head. The merge with `origin/main` (`a1ef0219e`) is clean (`git merge-tree`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test shared_face_bodies`: 5 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the heavy lane #1407).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_open_side`: 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: other suites (the delta touches one test only), ui suites, batch and heavy lanes.

## Judgement on "generates, then verify blocks the post"
I accept it here. It is not a blocker.
- The findings are real and come from the tool reach: 15 mm of flute and an 8 mm shank beside a 118 mm wall. The same R1 moves with a long-flute tool verify clean.
- No wrong G-code can be posted. All findings have `blocks_post: true` and the post is held by R1. The output is visible and never silent. The test pins this.
- The behaviour is on main. The takeover shows that a closed cavity gives the same kinds with the footprint law of main. The generate-then-hold design is the #722 design.
- The refusal of R1 on main came from the footprint (no 6 mm tool fit the eroded strip). It did not come from the tool reach. This PR removes that footprint refusal. It adds no new unsafe output. A refusal at generation for tool reach would be a new law for every 3D Pocket. It is correctly owed in #1844.
- Please do not treat "ok at generation" as "can post". The status `ok` on R1 comes with a held post. The decision file and the test comment say this.

## #1844
- The title, body, decision file and PR body agree (306 `shank_hit`, 30 `rapid_in_stock`, no gouge, defect on main, two design options).
- Labels: `bug`, `area:3d`, `source:agent`, `P3`, `effort:max`. `P3` fits the table: wrong behaviour with a workaround (a long-flute tool). `effort:max` fits the table: a collision law with an open design choice. It is above the safety floor (`effort:high` minimum). I did not change any label.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The body still says "full quick gate was not re-run on the final head". The delta is test and docs only, so this is acceptable.
- `generate.rs` is over 400 lines. The PR adds 11. The body already says that the split is owed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
